body:
Rule. Wrap a request as a command object with an execute (and maybe undo) so it can be stored, queued, or logged.

Why it matters. Bare function calls cannot sit on a queue or participate in undo without ad-hoc wrappers.

SAMPLE example. SAMPLE: an editor records InsertTextCommand objects; undo pops and reverses the last command rather than rebuilding the whole document.

When to use. Use when you need queueing, macros, audit logs, or undo of discrete actions.

When to refuse. Refuse command objects for every trivial setter with no queue or undo story.
